From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *diurnāta. Documented from 1283–5.[1] By surface analysis, jorn +‎ -ada.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [ʒurˈna.ðə]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [ʒorˈna.ðə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [d͡ʒoɾˈna.ða]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

jornada f (plural jornades)

  1. day
  2. day's walk
  3. (work) shift

Derived terms

[edit]
  • doble jornada
  • jornada de portes obertes
  • jornada diària
  • jornada escolar
  • jornada intensiva
  • jornada laboral
  • jornada nocturna
  • jornada partida
  • jornada plena

See also

[edit]
  • dia

References

[edit]
  • “jornada”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “jornada”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “jornada” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  1. ^ “jornada” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Occitan

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • jurnada (Limousin)
  • jornaa (Vivaro-Alpine)

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Occitan jornada, inherited from Vulgar Latin *diurnāta. Derivable from jorn +‎ -ada.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Limousin) IPA(key): /d͡ʒurˈnadɔ/, IPA(key): /d͡zurˈnadɔ/.
  • Audio (Béarn):(file)

Noun

[edit]

jornada f (plural jornadas)

  1. day, the period of one day

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese jornada, borrowed from Old Occitan jornada.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒoʁˈna.dɐ/ [ʒoɦˈna.dɐ]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒoʁˈna.dɐ/ [ʒoɦˈna.dɐ]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ʒoɾˈna.dɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ʒoʁˈna.dɐ/
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /ʒoɻˈna.dɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒoʁˈna.da/ [ʒoɦˈna.da]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʒuɾˈna.dɐ/ [ʒuɾˈna.ðɐ]

  • Hyphenation: jor‧na‧da

Noun

[edit]

jornada f (plural jornadas)

  1. journey; voyage (a long trip)
    Synonym: viagem
  2. a day’s travelling
  3. a day’s work

Further reading

[edit]
  • “jornada”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Spanish jornada, borrowed from Old Occitan jornada.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /xoɾˈnada/ [xoɾˈna.ð̞a]
  • Rhymes: -ada
  • Syllabification: jor‧na‧da

Noun

[edit]

jornada f (plural jornadas)

  1. day
    Synonym: día
  2. working day
    Synonym: jornada de trabajo
  3. short hike or journey
  4. day trip (especially a trip that must be completed in one day, for example due to lack of water en route)
  5. arduous trail
  6. act of a play

Derived terms

[edit]
  • al cabo de la jornada
  • al fin de la jornada
  • jornada de puertas abiertas
  • jornada de reflexión
  • jornada de trabajo (“working day”)
  • jornada electoral
  • jornadas f pl (“congress; conference”)

Related terms

[edit]
  • paraje

Further reading

[edit]
  • “jornada”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
